method: Each server: one discarded cold-start load (Vite dependency pre-optimization on a fresh worktree/server produces a one-time 7-9s artifact unrelated to the app), then 5 warm reloads. Same machine, same .env/Supabase backend for both servers, sequential (not concurrent) measurement.

navigation_timing_ms.interpretation: Exact head loads faster (lower loadEventEnd) at both median and p95 than the target-branch baseline for this scenario. Consistent with removing a full-width control-bar row (less to lay out above the fold).

dom_node_count_ready_gated.ready_gate: document.body.textContent.includes('verified properties'), plus a 2s settle for async map-tile loading
dom_node_count_ready_gated.interpretation: IMG (map tile) count is identical (25=25) between both, ruling out map-tile-loading timing as the cause of the total delta (unlike an earlier, less-settled sample in this same investigation, which showed a spurious IMG-driven gap). The real delta concentrates in SPAN (+47), path (+24), DIV (+26), svg (+15), circle (+5) — consistent with this PR's own explicit, intentional design change: the JourneySwitcher metadata-strip restyle from plain-text Chip pills to icon-per-item (MapPin/Building/TrendingUp, each a multi-path Lucide SVG) plus dot-separator spans. This is a deliberate, bounded visual-design cost approved as part of this PR's own scope, not a duplicate-mount defect (confirmed separately: discover-control-bar-row count is 0 on desktop; no duplicate DiscoverControlBar instances found).

bundle_size.all_other_chunks: byte-identical between baseline and exact head (vendor-react, vendor-leaflet, vendor-radix, vendor-supabase, vendor-recharts, DiscoverMapCanvas, etc.) — expected, since this PR touches none of that code
